payload.title: [blob-gc-4] Unbounded in-memory blob + object scan during GC pass (OOM DoS on large tenants)
payload.description:
AUDIT FINDING blob-gc-4 (medium/dos, confidence=medium, verify-votes +2/-0)

FILE: apps/server/src/blobs/gc-job.ts
LINES: 117-146, 170-171

WHAT: A GC pass loads every blob_metadata row for the tenant into a single array via listAllOldestFirst (line 170; blob-store.ts:187-196 has no LIMIT/OFFSET), and collectDeclaredReferencedBlobIds loads ALL objects of every ref-declaring object type via store.objects.list (line 135; object-store.ts:188-200 has no pagination) into memory, while also building a referenced Set of all ref values. For a tenant with millions of blobs/objects these full materializations coexist in heap simultaneously. There is no batching, streaming cursor, or row cap anywhere in the GC path.

IMPACT: On a large tenant, a single scheduled GC pass can exhaust worker memory and OOM-crash the process. Because the sweep is recurring, the crash can recur every interval, and a crash mid-pass (after some deletes) interacts with the recurring re-enqueue.

SUGGESTED FIX: Paginate both scans: stream blob_metadata oldest-first in bounded batches and resolve references per-batch (e.g. a targeted 'is this blobId referenced by any declared ref field' query) instead of materializing the full object set, or cap the number of blobs reclaimed per pass.
